title: Hosea Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 9.

questions.question: Why should Israel not rejoice for joy as other people do?
options: Because they have gone a whoring from their God
Because they are mourning a death
Because they have lost their possessions
Because they are celebrating a festival
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have gone a whoring from their God
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:1 states that Israel should not rejoice for joy because they have gone a whoring from their God.

questions.question: What will fail in Israel according to Hosea 9:2?
options: The new wine
The wheat harvest
The olive oil
The sheep flocks
questions.correctAnswer: The new wine
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:2 says the new wine shall fail in her, meaning the new wine will not sustain them.

questions.question: Where shall Ephraim return to according to Hosea 9:3?
options: Egypt
Babylon
Assyria
Philistia
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:3 states that Ephraim shall return to Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hosea 9:4, their sacrifices will be pleasing unto the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:4 explains that their sacrifices shall not be pleasing unto the LORD.

questions.question: What will their bread for their soul not do according to Hosea 9:4?
options: Come into the house of the LORD
Be eaten by the priests
Be blessed by the elders
Be given to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Come into the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:4 states their bread for their soul shall not come into the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What question does Hosea 9:5 ask about the solemn day and feast of the LORD?
options: What will ye do in the solemn day and in the day of the feast of the LORD?
Who will lead the feast of the LORD?
When will the feast of the LORD be celebrated?
Where shall the feast of the LORD be held?
questions.correctAnswer: What will ye do in the solemn day and in the day of the feast of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:5 asks what they will do in the solemn day and in the day of the feast of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:6, who shall gather up the people because of destruction?
options: Egypt
Babylon
Assyria
Philistia
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:6 says Egypt shall gather them up because of destruction.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:6 says that pleasant places for their silver will be possessed by nettles.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:6 mentions that nettles shall possess the pleasant places for their silver.

questions.question: Who shall bury them according to Hosea 9:6?
options: Memphis
The priests
The kings
The elders
questions.correctAnswer: Memphis
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:6 states Memphis shall bury them.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:1 indicates that Israel loved a reward upon every cornfloor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:1 specifically mentions Israel loved a reward upon every cornfloor.

questions.question: What will not feed them according to Hosea 9:2?
options: The floor and the winepress
The fields and the rivers
The mountains and the valleys
The sun and the rain
questions.correctAnswer: The floor and the winepress
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:2 says the floor and the winepress shall not feed them.

questions.question: What shall Ephraim eat in Assyria according to Hosea 9:3?
options: Unclean things
Clean and holy food
Bread from the altar
Manna from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Unclean things
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:3 states they shall eat unclean things in Assyria.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:5 asks about what they will do on the day of the feast of the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:5 asks 'What will ye do in the solemn day, and in the day of the feast of the LORD?'

questions.question: What shall be in their tabernacles according to Hosea 9:6?
options: Thorns
Gold
Clean water
Peace
questions.correctAnswer: Thorns
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:6 mentions thorns shall be in their tabernacles.

questions.question: In Hosea 9, which event comes first?
options: Israel going a whoring from their God
Ephraim returning to Egypt
Egypt gathering them up
Memphis burying them
questions.correctAnswer: Israel going a whoring from their God
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:1 mentions Israel going a whoring from their God before the other events mentioned in later verses.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:7, what is the reason given for the prophet being called a fool and the spiritual man mad?
options: The multitude of iniquity and great hatred
Their lack of knowledge
Their unbelief and stubbornness
The oppression of the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The multitude of iniquity and great hatred
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7 states that the prophet is a fool and the spiritual man mad because of the multitude of Israel's iniquity and the great hatred. This reflects the deep corruption and rebellion against God in the people (Hosea 9:7).

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:8 say about the prophet's role among Ephraim?
options: The prophet is a snare of a fowler in all his ways
The prophet faithfully leads Ephraim to God
The prophet is silent in the land
The prophet brings peace and healing
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet is a snare of a fowler in all his ways
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:8 describes the prophet as a snare of a fowler, indicating that the prophet entraps and misleads Ephraim. This illustrates the spiritual deception and corruption prevalent among Israel's leaders (Hosea 9:8).

questions.question: How does Hosea 9:9 describe Israel's moral state in comparison to past events?
options: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah
They have become righteous like the days of David
They have returned to the law of Moses
They have been faithful as in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:9 compares Israel’s deep corruption to the sinful days of Gibeah, a reference to grave moral failure in Israel’s history, showing persistent rebellion and sin (Hosea 9:9).

questions.question: What metaphor does Hosea 9:10 use to describe Israel before their sin?
options: Israel like grapes in the wilderness and fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree
Israel as a lion in the forest and fathers as mighty oaks
Israel as a flock of sheep and fathers as shepherds
Israel as rivers of water and fathers as mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Israel like grapes in the wilderness and fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:10 uses the imagery of grapes in the wilderness and the firstripe in the fig tree to depict the early purity and blessing of Israel before they turned to sin (Hosea 9:10).

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:11, what will happen to Ephraim's glory?
options: Their glory shall fly away like a bird from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception
Their glory shall increase and multiply
Their glory shall be established forever
Their glory shall rest upon their elders
questions.correctAnswer: Their glory shall fly away like a bird from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:11 declares that Ephraim’s glory will vanish swiftly and completely, like a bird flying away even before birth, symbolizing a total loss of blessing and fruitfulness (Hosea 9:11).

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 9:12 give for Ephraim bringing up children?
options: God will bereave them so that there shall not be a man left
Their children will become leaders
Their children will inherit the land
Their children will be blessed and multiply
questions.correctAnswer: God will bereave them so that there shall not be a man left
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:12 warns that though Ephraim may raise children, God will take them away so that no male offspring remains, indicating judgment and loss (Hosea 9:12).

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:7 teaches that the days of visitation and recompense are times Israel will not recognize.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7 states that Israel shall know the days of visitation and recompense, indicating awareness of God's judgment, not ignorance (Hosea 9:7).

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:8 indicates the watchman of Ephraim was with God, but prophets caused harm instead of help.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:8 contrasts the faithful watchman who was with God against the prophet who became a snare and caused hatred, showing corruption among leaders (Hosea 9:8).

questions.question: True or False: According to Hosea 9:9, God will ignore Israel's iniquity and sins because they have corrupted themselves deeply.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:9 says God will remember their iniquity and visit their sins, indicating that He will not ignore their corruption (Hosea 9:9).

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:10 say about Israel's fathers compared to their current separation unto shame?
options: They were like the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time
They were as rebellious as the current generation
They worshiped Baalpeor from the beginning
They were unfaithful from their youth
questions.correctAnswer: They were like the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:10 contrasts Israel’s fathers, who were like the early fruit of the fig tree (pure and promising), with the current generation who turned to Baalpeor and abominations (Hosea 9:10).

questions.question: How does Hosea 9:11-12 together depict the fate of Ephraim's offspring?
options: Their glory and offspring will be lost, and God will bereave them of children
Their offspring will prosper and multiply
Their children will be taken captive but return
Their glory will increase through their descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Their glory and offspring will be lost, and God will bereave them of children
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:11 describes Ephraim’s glory flying away like a bird from birth, and 9:12 states God will bereave them of children, showing complete loss of legacy and blessing (Hosea 9:11-12).

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:7-8, what is the relationship between Israel's iniquity and the condition of their prophets?
options: Because of iniquity, the prophet is a fool and a snare, causing hatred in God's house
The prophets remain faithful despite Israel’s sin
The prophets lead Israel to repentance
The prophets are uninvolved in Israel’s condition
questions.correctAnswer: Because of iniquity, the prophet is a fool and a snare, causing hatred in God's house
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7-8 links Israel’s multitude of iniquity to the folly and madness of prophets, who become snares and cause hatred, showing leadership failure due to sin (Hosea 9:7-8).

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience and consequences can a believer learn from Hosea 9:9-10?
options: Corruption leads to God remembering and visiting sin, despite initial blessings
Obedience guarantees no troubles
Sin is overlooked when the people are numerous
Faithfulness is irrelevant to God’s judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Corruption leads to God remembering and visiting sin, despite initial blessings
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:9-10 teach that despite God’s initial blessings on Israel’s fathers, deep corruption causes God to remember and punish their sins, emphasizing the importance of obedience (Hosea 9:9-10).

questions.question: Based on Hosea 9:11-12, what warning is given about trusting in family legacy or offspring?
options: Even if children are raised, God may take them away as a judgment
Family legacy guarantees God’s blessing
Offspring will protect from judgment
Children will always follow their parents’ faith
questions.correctAnswer: Even if children are raised, God may take them away as a judgment
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:12 warns that despite raising children, God can bereave them, showing that trust in offspring alone does not secure God’s favor (Hosea 9:12).

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:7-9 teach about the importance of spiritual leadership for obedience and integrity?
options: Corrupted prophets contribute to Israel’s iniquity and provoke God’s judgment
Spiritual leaders always protect Israel from sin
Prophets have no influence on the people's behavior
Good leaders can prevent all consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Corrupted prophets contribute to Israel’s iniquity and provoke God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7-9 shows that the folly and snares of prophets worsen Israel’s iniquity, leading to God’s visitation and judgment, underscoring the vital role of godly leadership (Hosea 9:7-9).

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:13, Ephraim is compared to what city, and what is the tragic fate of Ephraim's children?
options: Ephraim is compared to Tyrus, and his children will be brought to the murderer.
Ephraim is compared to Jerusalem, and his children will be exalted.
Ephraim is compared to Babylon, and his children will be taken captive.
Ephraim is compared to Nineveh, and his children will be prosperous.
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim is compared to Tyrus, and his children will be brought to the murderer.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:13 states, 'Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.' This shows a tragic contrast between prosperity and destruction.

questions.question: What does the plea to the Lord in Hosea 9:14 request as a consequence for Ephraim?
options: A miscarrying womb and dry breasts
Abundant harvest and prosperity
Peace and restoration
Strength and victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: A miscarrying womb and dry breasts
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:14 specifically asks, 'Give them, O LORD: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts,' indicating a judgment of barrenness.

questions.question: Where does Hosea say all the wickedness of Ephraim is found, and what is God's declared attitude there in Hosea 9:15?
options: In Gilgal, where God says He hated them and will drive them out.
In Jerusalem, where God promises restoration.
In Bethel, where God offers forgiveness.
In Samaria, where God remains silent.
questions.correctAnswer: In Gilgal, where God says He hated them and will drive them out.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:15 reads, 'All their wickedness is in Gilgal: for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more.' This expresses divine rejection.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:16, what has happened to Ephraim's root and fruit?
options: Their root is dried up and they shall bear no fruit.
Their root is strong and they will bear abundant fruit.
Their root is hidden but fruit is plentiful.
Their root is divided but fruit remains.
questions.correctAnswer: Their root is dried up and they shall bear no fruit.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:16 declares, 'Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit,' indicating judgment and cessation of prosperity.

questions.question: What ultimate fate does Hosea 9:17 predict for those who did not hearken to God?
options: They will be cast away and become wanderers among the nations.
They will be restored and blessed in their land.
They will be exalted above their enemies.
They will build new cities and prosper.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cast away and become wanderers among the nations.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:17 states, 'My God will cast them away, because they did not hearken unto him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations,' describing exile as a consequence of disobedience.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of barrenness as judgment found in Hosea 9:14?
options: Genesis 30:1 where Rachel asks for children.
Isaiah 54:1 where barren woman is promised many children.
Jeremiah 15:2 where childlessness is pronounced as judgment.
Psalm 23:1 with the theme of provision.
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 15:2 where childlessness is pronounced as judgment.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:2 speaks of barrenness and childlessness as a divine judgment, paralleling Hosea 9:14's plea for a miscarrying womb.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Hosea 9:11 where Ephraim's glory is described as flying away like a bird from birth, womb, and conception?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Simile
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:11 uses a simile comparing Ephraim's glory to a bird flying away, emphasizing loss from the earliest stages of life.

questions.question: In the historical context of Hosea 9, what does the reference to Ephraim returning to Egypt and eating unclean things in Assyria (Hosea 9:3) symbolize?
options: Political exile and spiritual defilement.
Prosperity and alliance with foreign nations.
Religious revival and purity.
Military conquest and victory.
questions.correctAnswer: Political exile and spiritual defilement.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:3 uses Egypt and Assyria to symbolize the coming exile and spiritual pollution due to Israel's unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Hosea 9:10 depict Israel before their fall, and what sin follows this depiction?
options: Israel is like grapes in the wilderness but then goes to Baalpeor and separates unto shame.
Israel is like a mighty tree but then worships the Lord alone.
Israel is a clean nation but then falls into idolatry of Egypt.
Israel is like a flowing river but then becomes dry.
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is like grapes in the wilderness but then goes to Baalpeor and separates unto shame.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:10 contrasts Israel's initial blessing with their later sin of idolatry at Baalpeor, highlighting covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:7 describes the prophet as wise and spiritually sound due to Israel's iniquity.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7 says, 'the prophet is a fool, the spiritual man is mad,' indicating corruption and confusion rather than wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 9:17 predicts that Israel will be wanderers among the nations because they did not listen to God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:17 clearly states that Israel will be cast away and wander among nations for failing to heed God's word.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of divine rejection and fruitlessness found in Hosea 9:16?
options: John 15:2 where branches that do not bear fruit are cut off.
Acts 2:1 about the Pentecost.
Romans 8:28 about all things working for good.
Revelation 21:4 about a new heaven and earth.
questions.correctAnswer: John 15:2 where branches that do not bear fruit are cut off.
questions.explanation: John 15:2 parallels Hosea 9:16's theme of fruitlessness and divine judgment by describing removal of unfruitful branches.

questions.question: What is the significance of Gilgal in Hosea 9:15, and how does it relate to Israel's covenant faithfulness?
options: Gilgal is the place where God first loved Israel, but now He hates their sins committed there.
Gilgal is a foreign city unrelated to Israel.
Gilgal is a place of victory and blessing for Israel.
Gilgal is where Israel's kings were crowned.
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal is the place where God first loved Israel, but now He hates their sins committed there.
questions.explanation: Gilgal was Israel's initial camp after entering Canaan (Joshua 4), symbolizing covenant beginnings, but Hosea 9:15 shows God's rejection due to their wickedness there.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew root meaning of the word translated as 'whoring' in Hosea 9:1 imply about Israel's relationship with God?
options: It implies spiritual adultery or unfaithfulness.
It implies physical illness.
It implies political alliance.
It implies joyful celebration.
questions.correctAnswer: It implies spiritual adultery or unfaithfulness.
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'zanah' used in Hosea 9:1 denotes spiritual adultery, indicating Israel's covenant unfaithfulness to God.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage does Hosea 9:9, referencing deep corruption like in the days of Gibeah, allude to, emphasizing Israel's moral decay?
options: Judges 19 where the depravity at Gibeah is described.
Genesis 6 describing the flood.
Exodus 20 listing the Ten Commandments.
1 Samuel 17 describing David and Goliath.
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 19 where the depravity at Gibeah is described.
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:9 points to the corrupt and violent events at Gibeah in Judges 19, underscoring Israel's moral degradation.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:1 indicate about Israel's relationship with God?
options: They have committed spiritual infidelity
They have remained faithful
They are rejoicing in God's blessings
They are in a covenant renewal ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: They have committed spiritual infidelity
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:1 states that Israel has 'gone a whoring from thy God', indicating their unfaithfulness and spiritual infidelity.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:4, how will the offerings of Israel be regarded by God?
options: Pleasing and acceptable
As the bread of mourners
As a sweet savor
As a sign of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: As the bread of mourners
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:4 explains that their sacrifices will be like 'the bread of mourners', indicating that they will be unacceptable and bring pollution rather than blessing.

questions.question: What fate is foretold for Ephraim in Hosea 9:3?
options: They will dwell in the LORD's land
They will return to Egypt
They will receive blessings from Assyria
They will conquer other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will return to Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:3 states that 'Ephraim shall return to Egypt', signifying punishment and exile due to their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: In Hosea 9:6, what does the text suggest will happen to those who are gathered by Egypt?
options: They will prosper abundantly
They will be buried in Memphis
They will return to the land of Israel
They will find refuge in Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: They will be buried in Memphis
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:6 indicates that 'Memphis shall bury them', illustrating the finality of their destruction and loss of life.

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:7 reveal about the state of the prophets during Israel's judgment?
options: They are wise and discerning
They are seen as fools and mad
They are leading the people to repentance
They are favored by God
questions.correctAnswer: They are seen as fools and mad
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7 describes the prophets as 'a fool' and 'mad', reflecting the confusion and moral decay present in Israel due to their iniquity.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:10, how did God find Israel?
options: Like a barren tree
Like grapes in the wilderness
Like a mighty fortress
Like a lost sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Like grapes in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:10 states that God found Israel 'like grapes in the wilderness', indicating a time of potential fruitfulness that was ultimately corrupted.

questions.question: What is the significance of Ephraim's glory in Hosea 9:11?
options: It will increase abundantly
It will fly away like a bird
It will be established forever
It will be a source of pride
questions.correctAnswer: It will fly away like a bird
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:11 metaphorically states that Ephraim's glory will 'fly away like a bird', suggesting a swift and irreversible loss of honor and status.

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:12 indicate about the consequences of Israel's sin?
options: They will be blessed with many children
They will suffer bereavement
They will experience great joy
They will return to their homeland
questions.correctAnswer: They will suffer bereavement
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:12 states that 'I will bereave them', indicating the severe consequences of sin, including loss of children and family.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:15, where is all their wickedness located?
options: In Jerusalem
In Gilgal
In Egypt
In Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: In Gilgal
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:15 specifies that 'all their wickedness is in Gilgal', indicating a central location of idolatry and sin that has provoked God's wrath.

questions.question: What does Hosea 9:16 reveal about Ephraim's fruitfulness?
options: They will bear much fruit
Their root is dried up
They will flourish like a tree
They will be a blessing to many
questions.correctAnswer: Their root is dried up
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:16 states that 'Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up', indicating a complete lack of spiritual vitality and productivity due to their sins.

questions.question: What will happen to those who do not heed God's warnings according to Hosea 9:17?
options: They will be gathered to safety
They will be cast away by God
They will be blessed
They will find peace
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cast away by God
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:17 states that 'My God will cast them away', emphasizing the dire consequences of ignoring God's call and commands.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's judgment is illustrated in Hosea 9:7-9?
options: God's judgment is always merciful
God's judgment is inevitable and just
God's judgment is arbitrary
God's judgment does not affect His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is inevitable and just
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:7-9 reflects the certainty of God's judgment for the iniquity of Israel, demonstrating His justice in punishing their sins.

questions.question: How does Hosea 9:1-2 connect to the broader theme of idolatry in Israel?
options: It shows God's approval of their practices
It highlights their infidelity and impending judgment
It emphasizes God's unchanging love
It illustrates their prosperity and blessings
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights their infidelity and impending judgment
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:1-2 points to Israel's infidelity through idolatry and the resulting judgment, a recurring theme throughout the book of Hosea.

questions.question: What insight do Hosea 9:10 and 12 collectively provide about God's relationship with Israel?
options: God desires to bless them abundantly
God acknowledges their repentance
God's judgment will lead to bereavement and loss
God has forgotten His covenant with them
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment will lead to bereavement and loss
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:10 and 12 together illustrate that Israel's unfaithfulness leads to God's judgment, resulting in bereavement and suffering.

questions.question: How does Hosea 9:14 reflect God's attribute of justice?
options: God will provide abundance
God will inflict judgment as a response to sin
God will ignore wickedness
God will bless the unfaithful
questions.correctAnswer: God will inflict judgment as a response to sin
questions.explanation: Hosea 9:14, where God asks for a 'miscarrying womb and dry breasts', indicates His justice in responding to Israel's unfaithfulness with severe consequences.
